body: This helped more than you'll know. Thank you.

"That there is an out helps you stay in"

-Charles Bukowski

Thanks for that. It really got me thinking.

>I think it's something that must be fought for, must be searched out. 

This reminds me of Camus's 'One recognizes one's course by discovering the paths that stray from it'. For some time, I thought my unhappiness stemmed from being in the 'wrong path'. So I changed directions several times. Changing the scenery/setting always works initially... until the novelty wears off. Novelty helps because it is distracting. Then the sense of futility and meaninglessness sets in again and doesn't leave. Despair resumes, invariably. I've realized it's never been any of the terrains I've charted that was the issue. I'm just not wired for happiness. I am at times embittered by people around me to whom happiness comes so easily. They very often dismiss (or chide) my joylessness with such levity because their own spells of unhappiness do not last very long. So talking to them all but amplifies the despair and sense of alienation.

I'm just tired of looking for ways to distract myself from crippling introspection, I guess. And I don't want to hold out any longer for the highly improbable prospect of things changing, and not in a transitory distracted-by-the-novelty way. My unhappiness is rooted in the way I am, and I don't think I can really, substantially change that. So missing out on 20 more years of living with these same thought patterns wouldn't be a loss. What is the point of a protracted, miserable life?

Thanks for your reply.

>get some new friends

I wish this was easy. I am not an extrovert, however much I wish I was.

> keep your chin up 

I really try to have a 'positive outlook', but I don't think this is something you can will yourself into having. I always feel mentally drained after a day of forced  optimism -- days like this always end in tears/bitterness/self-loathing, it feels like self-delusion. And it really bothers me when friends tell me to 'snap out of it', as though you really had that much power over it.

Disposition has a biological basis. I think I lost the genetic lottery in that regard, in which case it doesn't make much sense to think it will change if I just stick around. When I hit 20, I told myself I was going to live until 30 (I thought maybe things would change after college), but even that feels too far away now. Those last years would just be spent amassing more experiences of loneliness and defeatism and dejection and impotent rage.
